title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 4

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the PLC workshop take place?
tasks.audioText: The PLC documentation workshop will take place on Tuesday at one fifteen in the control systems room. Students should bring the sample input-output table. The instructor will explain how input and output addresses are listed and why the controller model should be included in the document. The exercise will use a printed example only.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which PLC address table is required for the documentation workshop?
tasks.audioText: The PLC documentation workshop will take place on Tuesday at one fifteen in the control systems room. Students should bring the sample input-output table. The instructor will explain how input and output addresses are listed and why the controller model should be included in the document. The exercise will use a printed example only.

tasks.prompt: A programmable logic controller uses a programme to process input information and control outputs. Its documentation may include an input-output list, a description of programme sections and the controller model. Address formats can vary between systems. For that reason, students should use the documentation for the specific controller rather than assume that every PLC uses identical address conventions. Reading 1. What may PLC documentation include?
options: An input-output list, programme-section description and controller model

tasks.prompt: Why should students check the specific controller model?
options: Because address formats can vary between systems

tasks.prompt: The controller model ___ in the technical document.
Choose TWO items that may appear in PLC documentation.
A device used to control industrial processes according to a programme is a programmable logic ___.
You are unsure about an input address. What should you ask?
options: I will use an address from another controller.
Could we check the input address in the documentation for this PLC model?
I will change the address without review.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of PLC documentation in a logical order.
options: Record the reference in the document
correctOrder: Record the reference in the document

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why PLC documentation should identify the controller model and include a clear input-output list.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
